claims.text: The as-deposited coatings are approximately 1 μm thick.
The Al-Cr-Fe-Ni multilayers contain FCC and BCC phases.
The coatings are produced from Al0.2CrFeNi and Al targets.
A 16 nm modulation period produces semicoherent FCC/BCC interfaces.
The 8 nm multilayer has coherent interfaces.
The 32 and 80 nm multilayers are dominated by grain-boundary interfaces.
Semicoherent FCC/BCC interfaces in the 16 nm multilayer contain misfit dislocations.
Semicoherent interfaces block dislocation glide.
Blocked dislocation glide produces localized dislocation pileups.
Misfit dislocations and dislocation pileups generate high localized interfacial stress.
High localized interfacial stress promotes interfacial amorphization.
Interfacial amorphization increases free volume and structural disorder.
The increased free volume and disorder lower atomic-migration barriers.
Lower atomic-migration barriers facilitate diffusion- or interface-slip-mediated deformation.
Interfacial amorphization shifts creep from dislocation slip or climb to diffusion- or interface-slip-mediated deformation.
The proposed shift in creep mechanism explains the enhanced room-temperature creep resistance of the 16 nm multilayer.
The 16 nm multilayer will have a lower creep strain rate than the 8, 32, and 80 nm multilayers.
The 16 nm multilayer will have a creep stress exponent around 1–2.
The 8, 32, and 80 nm multilayers will have higher creep rates than the 16 nm multilayer.
Stress exponents around 1–2 diagnose diffusion or interface-slip creep, whereas exponents above 3 diagnose dislocation-mediated creep.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says amorphization lowers migration barriers and facilitates diffusion or interface slip, which promotes time-dependent deformation, but the predicted outcome attributes a lower creep rate and enhanced creep resistance to that same facilitation. No additional rate-limiting step is given to resolve the reversed causal direction.

The falsification rule describes stress-induced interfacial amorphization as the rate-limiting factor for creep, while the mechanism describes amorphization as lowering barriers and facilitating deformation rather than limiting its rate.
